tuition.assumptions: Conservative tuition-only planning ceiling for the ordinary three-semester Standard MS ECE in Pittsburgh; the extended, intensive-project and other-campus options are outside this scope.

The ECE admissions FAQ directs Professional MS students to the College of Engineering current tuition page. That page gives a 2026-27 Masters rate of USD 30,755 per fall/spring semester, with a separate USD 855 per-unit rate.

Three full semester charges give a ceiling of USD 92,265 at that published reference rate. A permitted reduced final load may cost less; no minimum or exact bill is asserted. The university warns that departmental actual rates can vary and must be confirmed before a commitment.
Future rate increases, summer or extended study, additional courses, fees, insurance and living costs are excluded. This does not assume a scholarship or assistantship.

directory_policies.notes.8: Cost context: Published-reference tuition ceiling USD 92,265 for the ordinary three-semester Pittsburgh Standard MS. The ECE FAQ points to the engineering tuition page; actual departmental bills and future rates still require confirmation.
directory_policies.notes.9: Preparation: The department welcomes applicants without an ECE background and sets no universal course-by-course entry cutoff here. Individual readiness and prerequisite equivalency remain university decisions.
directory_policies.notes.10: Other eligibility: Reviewed ordinary application checklist: application/fee, purpose statement, CV, three letters, all transcripts and applicable English reports. GRE is optional for Fall 2027. Submission, equivalency and admission are not asserted.

fact_summary: The ECE FAQ links its current tuition source, lists a complete ordinary application checklist and welcomes applicants without an ECE background. It does not impose a universal entry-course list; English score floors still lack complete validity review.
